clue.text: With chores unfinished, wife in temper cleans jug

indicators.note: a task left unfinished loses its final stage, so the last letter of the synonym for chores goes

parts.note: chores are household work

indicators.note: the wife is placed in the middle of the word for temper

parts.note: a temper or humour is a mood
to clean hard is to scrub, so cleans gives scrubs

explanation.surface: A wife with housework left half done, in a bad mood, scours a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is slang for prison, not a pitcher. WORMWOOD SCRUBS is a well-known prison in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Jug is old British slang for a prison, and this is a famous London jail.

clue.text: Spring off, clutching weapon, unlikely to fall

parts.note: a spring of water is a well

indicators.note: the word for off holds the weapon tightly within it

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: A water source has gone foul around a spear yet stays standing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with its weight evenly distributed is stable, so it is unlikely to topple over.

clue.text: City dweller heading for rolling country

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of rolling is used

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A townsman sets off towards hilly countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is Rome, the Eternal City; a dweller there is a Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of Rome, the ancient city, is called by this demonym.

clue.text: Success for one girl showing flute?

parts.note: to succeed is to win
for one means for example, abbreviated e.g.
lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A victory for a young woman playing the flute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flute' looks like the instrument but is a tall slender glass for champagne; the question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A champagne flute is one kind of stemmed drinking vessel for wine.

clue.text: Unit showing strength in field from old desert battles

indicators.note: letters that battle fight among themselves and end up jumbled

explanation.surface: A military unit proving its might in the field during old desert wars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' suggests a battlefield, but here it is a magnetic field.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is the CGS unit measuring the intensity of a magnetic field.

clue.text: Hint — it's two things found in can

parts.note: soup is something sold in a tin can
can is slang for prison, where a con, a convict, is found

explanation.surface: A tip about what you might find inside a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' does double duty: a tin holds soup, and the slang sense prison holds a con (convict).
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny trace or suggestion, so a hint of flavour or feeling.

clue.text: Traveller not so rainswept after lowering head

indicators.note: in a down entry the head is the top letter; lowering it moves that letter further down the word

parts.note: less wet means drier

explanation.surface: A traveller, less soaked than before, ducks their head.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider travels on horseback, a bike or a bus, so is a kind of passenger or journeyer.

clue.text: A toff backed to secure Republican victory, like George W Bush?

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the Republican in place inside them
backed means turned back, so the words a toff are read in reverse order

parts.note: a nob is a toff, an upper-class person
a win is a gain

explanation.surface: An upper-class figure supporting a Republican win, in the style of the former US president.
explanation.walkthrough: George W Bush described himself as a born-again Christian, so the question mark flags him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has had a renewed religious conversion, as Bush famously claimed, is so described.

clue.text: Getting knocked back, call Latin lover

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word for call is read in reverse

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A Latin lover gets rebuffed when phoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Leman is an archaic word for a sweetheart or paramour.

clue.text: Game played at Her Majesty's residence?

definitions.text: Game played at Her Majesty's residence?

parts.words: Game played at Her Majesty's residence?
parts.note: a game round at the Queen's place could be called ..., ER being Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A sport enjoyed at the royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: To go round someone's is to visit their home; ER is the Queen, so round ER's is a game at her residence. Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a bat-and-ball team sport, long played in British schools and parks.

clue.text: Sick nurse taught for free

indicators.note: something sick is out of order, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taught means trained

explanation.surface: An ailing nurse is educated at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained means unchecked or unconfined, hence at liberty.

clue.text: Obscure British film screening in the vicinity

indicators.note: a screen shields what lies within, so the film's title wraps the other piece

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial
nigh means near, in the vicinity

explanation.surface: A little-known British film being shown locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective but is a verb: to darken.
explanation.definitionFit: To benight is to plunge into darkness, so to cloud over or make dim.

clue.text: Hanging a scoundrel, endlessly corrupt

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man

indicators.note: without its end the word for corrupt loses its final letter

parts.note: to corrupt is to taint

explanation.surface: Executing a villain who is utterly crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests the gallows but is the noun: a drape.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a fabric drape hung at a window, a wall hanging.

clue.text: With heart not in lechery, back away from call girl

indicators.note: with its heart gone, only the outside letters of lechery are kept
the back of the word for call, its last letter, is taken away

parts.note: to call on the phone is to dial

explanation.surface: Losing her appetite for lust, a woman retreats from a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female first name, as in Lydia Bennet of Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Run below hills and fall

indicators.note: in a down entry the run piece is placed below the hills piece

parts.note: the downs are rolling chalk hills in southern England
to lope is to run with long strides

explanation.surface: A runner heads down from the hills and tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are areas of open chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall in the ground is a descending incline, a slope going down.

clue.text: In speech, fool gets foolish in Shakespearean location

indicators.note: spoken aloud the word for fool gives a sound we spell differently

parts.note: a dunce is a fool
inane means foolish

explanation.surface: When talking, an idiot sounds idiotic in a Shakespeare setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunsinane is the hill where Macbeth meets his end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunsinane, the Scottish hill and castle in Macbeth, is a setting of that play.

clue.text: During one month, love unusual and improper behaviour

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
Dec is the abbreviation for December
love is zero in tennis, written O
rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: For a month, romance and odd conduct go together.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, conduct that breaks good manners.

clue.text: Different way to enter beach? Sun could be here

parts.note: new means different, as in a new approach

indicators.note: the way goes into the middle of the beach word

parts.note: a beach is sand
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A fresh path onto the beach, where the sun might shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is not the star but The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper sold at a newsagent's kiosk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a newspaper, and a kiosk selling papers would stock it.

clue.text: Salutation with special function in ancient language

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A greeting with a particular role in an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the old Iranian tongue of the Zoroastrian scriptures.

clue.text: Take away shipment finally transported to the North

indicators.note: in a down entry going north is going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top
finally picks the last letter of shipment

parts.note: carted means transported

explanation.surface: Removing the last of a shipment hauled up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take away' looks like a removal but means detract, as in to take away from someone's achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to diminish or subtract from something's worth.

clue.text: Gathering fruitcake for snack in diner?

parts.note: a do is a party or gathering
a fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, a nut

explanation.surface: A party serves cake as a snack at a roadside eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitcake' means a madman, not a cake. The diner points to the American spelling DONUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut, spelt the American way, is a typical sweet snack in a US diner.

clue.text: South African maybe putting greenery in set location

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
a tree is a piece of greenery

explanation.surface: A South African golfer putting by the trees on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' joins the pieces and nods to golf. Elstree is home to famous film and TV studios north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree is known for its film studios, so a place where sets are built for filming.

clue.text: Le Père Goriot: somewhat revolting fellow!

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters read backwards
somewhat means only part of the title is used

explanation.surface: A verdict that the hero of a Balzac novel is a rather disgusting man.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is a man's name, so any one chap or fellow.

clue.text: It's played in two acts, with nothing amiss

indicators.note: amiss means wrong, so these letters are out of order
two calls for a pair of copies of the word for acts

parts.note: an act is a deed
nothing is zero, written O

explanation.surface: A play staged in two acts that goes without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two acts' asks for ACT twice; with O those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, something performed by a musician.

clue.text: Gondola's back alongside vessel in gulf

indicators.note: the back of Gondola is its final letter

parts.note: by means beside, alongside
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: The stern of a Venetian boat next to a ship in a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gulf' suggests a sea bay, but it means a deep chasm.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a bottomless chasm, a yawning gap or void.

clue.text: Place with cross, gloomy rocker plugging a record for spinning

indicators.note: the rocker plugs the gap, going into the middle of the other piece
something spun turns round, so a and the word for record are read backwards

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log
a goth is a fan of dark, gloomy rock music

explanation.surface: A grumpy goth fan pushes a record to be played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' sounds like promoting a record, but it means filling a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Golgotha is the hill outside Jerusalem where Christ was crucified.

clue.text: Light running clothes could be made from this

definitions.text: clothes could be made from this

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Lightweight running kit might be made of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fabric from cellulose, used to make garments.

clue.text: Wilde gutted, play done with amateurs getting haughty verdict

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters
play means to fool about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde, crushed, as amateurs finish a play and give a snooty review.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is attributed to Queen Victoria as a royal snub.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's supposed royal snub is the classic example of a lofty disapproving judgement.
